title: PRD traffic-light clearance matrix and owning-eviction policy for cross-team reviews
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: PRD reviews currently create long, uncoordinated review loops across Eng/Design/Legal. Decisions are binary (approve/reject) and leave teams guessing about partial readiness and who owns follow-ups. Goal: introduce a lightweight 'traffic-light' clearance matrix (Green/Amber/Red) per review area plus a formal owning-eviction policy so an owner is always accountable for moving amber items to green or escalating on schedule.
scope: Define traffic-light definitions for Design, Engineering, Legal, Security, and Product
Create per-area acceptance rubrics (what qualifies as Green/Amber/Red)
Define owning-eviction policy and grace periods for Amber items
Integrate the matrix into PRD reviews and the PRD signoff checklist in Confluence
Add minimal Console dashboard view for PRD clearance status (per PRD, per area)
out_of_scope: Full automation of signoffs (this is a tooling + process change, not a platform change)
Large UI rewrites of Console — only a small status widget is required for MVP
Rewriting legal templates; we will reference existing agreed clauses
acceptance_criteria: Traffic-light definitions documented in Confluence and linked from PRD template
Per-area rubrics exist and are reviewed by at least one owner from Engineering, Design, and Legal
Owning-eviction policy published and agreed by stakeholders (includes timelines: 3-day owner action window, 7-day escalation)
A lightweight PRD Clearance widget in Confluence with Green/Amber/Red per area for MVP
At least two upcoming PRD reviews use the matrix and we capture feedback in a follow-up retro
